title: Unbounded affine-plane classes and actual radical-curve recovery

newly_cached_primary_context.role: Context only: Introduction and Theorems1-3 concern inequivalent affine-space embeddings in quadrics of dimension2 and3; no four-quadric class formula or rectification is imported.
Context only: abstract, equivariant grading hypotheses and Theorem3.2; no grading is assumed for the actual embedding or imported as a closure.

retained_external_foundations.statement: Integral cycle map, principal-divisor rational equivalence, proper homotopies and compact sphere pairing; foundational source bytes remain pinned through IW.

Explicit retained Abhyankar-Moh-Suzuki rectification of an actual closed affine line in the complex plane, stated in Jelonek2011.03472v3 Theorem2.4. The broader input is reused, not the narrower Keller-component scope of GR0.
Gwozdziewicz Theorem1.1, Keller injectivity on one affine line forces inverse.
Qualitative Jelonek-Lason1411.5011v2 Theorem3.2 and the retained normalization/Hurwitz argument identify polynomially parametric curve components with affine normalization A1.

retained_structural_inputs.statement: Full constant normal-trace chart closure and retained Keller denominator removal.
No abelian Galois intermediate field; source divisor domination and square-free nonconstant target pullbacks.

direct_proof_arguments: A geometric-series polynomial recovers t from e_m for every m; a principal divisor has exact multiplicity m on the unwanted plane.
Explicit quadric rotations and principal-divisor relations determine the class sign, giving all integers and a class-zero closed plane.
In the total quadric-level family the fibre plane is itself a principal divisor on a threefold, even with the critical level removed.
The actual closed zero-section gives R=C[f,y1,y2]; its exact first free jet gives R/(f)=C[K mod f].
An actual A1 component is rectified in the source plane before applying the retained Keller one-line theorem.
A descended square would give a forbidden quadratic intermediate field unless f already descends; coprime pullbacks remove denominators.
The closed radical curve hits every component of the target zero curve and is isomorphic to it.
A singleton source fibre at every zero target forces that whole curve into the nonproperness set under hypothetical degree greater than one.
Qualitative nonproperness uniruledness forces A1 normalization, while any smooth component would be an actual A1 and force the inverse.
The actual cotangent critical equations give one critical point for every target perturbation on that zero curve.
